title: Following up on the Pine Script optimizer post - a deeper look at our Research Agent (with a real example)
author: vitaliy3commas
selftext:
A while back I shared the Pine Script strategy optimizer we built. A few people asked what else the platform does, so here's a closer look at the part I use most: the Research Agent.

The idea: instead of searching the web and getting an article back, you ask a market question in plain language and the agent pulls historical and live data from connected sources (on-chain, news, price, DeFi), analyses it, and hands back dashboards and findings built on actual numbers.

Here's a real run. I asked: "If the Fear & Greed Index is ≤ 20 (extreme fear) and I buy BTC, what's historically been the optimal holding period?" What came back, over the last 3 years:

* FNG hit ≤ 20 on 24 days (2.2% of the period), clustered into 6 distinct episodes, each tied to a real macro shock (SEC/rate fears 2023, the Aug 2024 global crash, the 2025 post-ATH correction, the Apr 2025 tariff shock).
* 7-day hold: +0.14% vs +1.13% baseline - actually underperforms, the signal is noise short-term.
* 30-day hold: +8.05% vs +5.86% baseline - +2.2pp edge, 58% win rate.
* 90-day hold: +43.66% vs +21.57% baseline - +22.1pp edge.

Now the important caveat, and the reason I'm showing this example specifically: that 90-day line had a 100% win rate across the 24 days - but that's a *perfect in-sample* rate, and those 24 days are really \~6 independent episodes, not 24. So the honest read isn't "this is a 100%-win strategy." It's "extreme fear has historically been an accumulation window that needed \~2-3 months to pay off, not a same-week bounce." The agent flags the correlation too (FNG vs 30-day forward return ≈ -0.31).

That's the point I want to make about the tool: it's a research and insight engine, not a strategy generator. It finds you the edge and shows the caveats - turning that into an actual traded strategy is still your job (and a separate part of the platform). It's not going to hand you a finished system from one question.

Under the hood it runs on partnership data providers plus a proprietary data warehouse, so even free users get recent data; you can plug in your own API keys for more depth. Charts come with every answer.

Live strategy execution and Telegram alerts on research conditions are rolling out soon, not live yet.

Happy to answer questions about how the research or data sourcing works.

Disclosure: I'm on the team behind QuantPilot, so this is me showing our own tool, not an unbiased review.
